ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Act on Reporting and Use of Specific Financial Transaction Information (Act No. 16566, as last amended by Act No. 18480; arts. 4-6, 11-2, and 31), its Enforcement Decree (Presidential Decree No. 32296), the Prohibition of Financing of Offenses of Public Pressure Act (Act No. 17484), the Financial Services Commission's Regulations on Customer Due Diligence and Identification of Beneficial Owners (FSC Notice No. 2021-7), and the FATF-aligned AML/CFT guidelines of the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: District Court Registration Office, Supreme Court of Korea
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For use in an Apostille Convention state: original certificate issued by the court registry and then apostilled by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea. For use in a non-member state: original certificate certified by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and then legalized by the consular section of the destination state in Korea. The apostille and consular legalization routes are mutually exclusive and must never be chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Certified Corporate Registry Extract equivalent)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Local District Court Registry / Internet Registration Office (IROS)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path: certified registry extract apostilled by the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Consular Legalization path: certified registry extract authenticated by the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs and then legalized at the destination country's consulate in Korea. The two paths are alternatives, never sequential.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Korean Notary Public appointed under the Notary Public Act
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarize the corporate board resolution and power of attorney, then either (i) obtain a Hague Apostille from the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs for Apostille Convention jurisdictions, or (ii) obtain MOFA certification and then consular legalization at the destination country's embassy/consulate for non-member jurisdictions. Do not apply both routes.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: District Court Registration Office or the registering Notary Public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille route: certified true copy apostilled by the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs for Hague-member destination states. Consular route: certified true copy authenticated by the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs and then legalized by the destination state's consulate in Korea. The routes are parallel and mutually exclusive.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter for the Charitable Endowment Account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed commercial bank in the Republic of Korea
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Bank letter on letterhead, signature confirmed, notarized if required, then either apostilled by MOFA for Hague states or, for non-Hague states, certified by MOFA and legalized by the destination consulate; the two paths cannot be combined.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Tax Clearance Certificate and Non-Arrearage Confirmation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National Tax Service of the Republic of Korea
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Original tax certificate apostilled by the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs for Apostille Convention states; alternatively, for non-member states, the original certificate is certified by MOFA and then legalized by the destination country's consulate in Korea. Use only the applicable route.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before formation, each shareholder, director, officer, and ultimate beneficial owner must be identified and verified using government-issued identity documents, corporate registry extracts, and source-of-funds evidence. Mandatory screening must run continuously against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, Korean domestic designations under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, and the Korean Financial Intelligence Unit's own screening list. Enhanced due diligence applies to all PEPs, their family members, and close associates as defined by FATF, including foreign, domestic, and international-organization PEPs, with documented source of wealth and funds. Automated rescreening is required at least quarterly and before every grant distribution or wire transfer; any confirmed or fuzzy positive match requires an immediate suspicious transaction report to the Korean FIU, a provisional funds freeze under the Proceeds of Crime Act, and escalation to the compliance officer.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Internet Registration Office (IROS) of the Supreme Court of Korea
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Korean Commercial Act and Commercial Registration Enforcement Rules, a Yuhan Hoesa must bear a Hangul trade name ending with the statutory suffix 'Yuhan Hoesa' (meaning limited company); foreign-language words must be rendered in a phonetic Hangul transliteration that matches the intended pronunciation. Hanja or Latin-script words may be appended parenthetically if not misleading. The four-tier naming convention is (i) optional distinguishing brand token, (ii) core trade name in Hangul, (iii) mandatory business-type suffix 'Yuhan Hoesa', and (iv) optional statutory business objective descriptor. The proposed name must not be identical or misleadingly similar to any name already registered in the same registry or to any name protected by a third-party goodwill right.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 30 days from the registry's written refusal, the applicant shall submit an objection petition to the head of the district court registration office, attaching the proposed Hangul name, English transliteration, ISIC 6430 activity description, and evidence that no identical or misleadingly similar name exists. If refused, the applicant may file a reconsideration or immediate appeal under the Non-Contentious Case Procedure Act, or amend the trade name and re-file. A rejection notice does not automatically extend the name reservation; the applicant must perfect a new reservation or registration application before the prior reservation lapses.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox-only address is generally accepted for routine commercial registration but is likely to be rejected in this charitable endowment sector by the National Tax Service and supervised financial institutions. Under the Commercial Act and tax laws, a company must maintain a place of business at the registered address where corporate records, accounting books, and grant-making documents are accessible. Banks applying FATF-compliant customer due diligence require a physical office, lease agreement, utility invoice, and a responsible representative who can attend an on-site visit. For an ISIC 6430 endowment-management entity seeking tax-exempt status and grant distribution authority, a pure virtual mailbox will not satisfy commercial substance requirements; the registered office must be a dedicated physical suite with signage, staffed business hours, and original records available for inspection.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000, as amended), Articles 287-2 through 287-74 on Yuhan Hoesa (limited liability company), together with the Commercial Registration Act, Supreme Court Regulations on Commercial Registration, Civil Act Article 32 on public-interest legal persons, and the Act on Establishment and Operation of Public Interest Corporations
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Registration Division of the District Court Registry Office, National Court Administration of the Republic of Korea, being the registry of the district court with territorial jurisdiction over the Company's registered office, including the Seoul Central District Court Registry office if the office is located in Seoul
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Limited Liability Company (Yuhan Hoesa) filed under the Commercial Registration Act, accompanied by the notarized Articles of Incorporation
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is required for a Yuhan Hoesa under the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea. Contributions must, however, be paid in full before or at the time of the incorporation registration, and each member's contribution must be accurately recorded in the Articles of Incorporation and the capital contribution schedule. No blocked escrow account is mandated by the Companies Act for ordinary incorporation. If the company will hold donated or endowed assets for charitable purposes, the competent public-interest supervisory ministry may require the endowment assets to be deposited into a dedicated bank account or trust account held in the name of YUHANG HOESA and maintained blocked until the public-interest establishment authorization is issued.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS RESOLUTION OF YUHANG HOESA (LLC), a limited liability company organized under the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, with its registered office in Seoul, Republic of Korea. ADOPTED on [Date] by the unanimous written consent of the Board of Directors. WHEREAS the incorporators have resolved to form a Yuhan Hoesa for the purpose of endowment management for philanthropic and scientific grants under ISIC 6430, and have subscribed to the contributed capital set forth in the subscription schedule; WHEREAS the Commercial Act requires full payment of contributions, designation of a registered office, appointment of statutory officers, and opening of a corporate banking relationship; NOW THEREFORE the Board of Directors hereby resolves as follows: 1. Capital Subscription and Payment. Each director and member acknowledges the accuracy of the capital contribution schedule, declares that every contribution has been or will be paid in full to the Company's designated bank account prior to the completion of commercial registration, and authorizes the Executive Director to issue all payment instructions and to record the contributed capital in the statutory accounting books. 2. Banking Authorization. The bank account maintained at [Bank] and [Branch], with account number [xxxx], shall be the primary corporate and endowment account. The Executive Director and Compliance Officer are jointly authorized to open, operate, and close bank accounts, to sign wire transfer forms, to execute electronic banking agreements, and to initiate board-approved grant distributions, provided that any payment exceeding KRW [threshold] requires two authorized signatures. 3. Registered Office Adoption. The address located at [Full address], Seoul, Republic of Korea is hereby adopted as the Company's registered office, and all legal notices, regulatory service of process, and official correspondence shall be delivered to that address. 4. Appointment of Officers. [Name] is appointed Executive Director with authority to represent the Company; [Name] is appointed Chief Financial Officer; [Name] is appointed Compliance Officer; and [Name] is appointed Corporate Secretary. Each officer shall have the duties and authorities provided by the Commercial Act, the Articles of Incorporation, and this Resolution. 5. Further Actions. The officers are authorized and directed to execute all documents, to make all registrations, to pay all fees, to obtain the necessary public-interest foundation authorization, business registration certificate, and any tax-exemption approval, and to take every lawful measure to carry out this Resolution. This resolution shall be binding on the Company and may be amended only by a subsequent resolution of the Board. Adopted this [day] of [month], [year].

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft, Execute, and Notarize the Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Korean Notary Public under the Notary Act, with counsel from a Korean licensed attorney in the Commercial Registration practice
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Articles of Incorporation of YUHANG HOESA in Korean, including the corporate purpose, exact contribution amounts, registered office address, representation method, officer composition, and disposition of residual assets for public interest upon dissolution. All incorporators must sign and seal the articles. The notary verifies legal capacity, actual presence, and legality of purpose under the Civil Act and the Commercial Act. The notarized original is required for the court registry. Any purely philanthropic purpose must also be consistent with the Act on Establishment and Operation of Public Interest Corporations before the public-interest authorization step.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Incorporation in the Korean language
Notarization fee receipt
Personal identification cards and individual seal certificates of all incorporators
Power of attorney if any incorporator signs through a proxy
Registered office address proof or proposed address consent letter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary raises a defect or refuses notarization, amend the Articles and have all incorporators re-execute the revised text before the notary. If the proposed company name conflicts with an existing registration, reserve an alternative name and submit a new name confirmation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Subscribe and Pay Contributions and Establish a Dedicated Endowment Account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: The designated commercial bank approved by the incorporators, and the competent public-interest ministry if an endowment escrow condition is imposed
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary or special bank account in the name of YUHANG HOESA through the designated bank, clearly designating the account as a capital contribution or endowment trust account if the Company will hold endowed assets. Each member shall remit or deposit in full the capital contribution subscribed in the Articles. For charitable endowment funds, the competent supervising ministry may require the funds to remain blocked until the public-interest establishment permit is granted. Obtain a certificate of deposit balance from the bank; the court registry shall receive evidence of cash contribution to avoid a defect on registration. All deposits must match exactly the capital schedule; in-kind contributions require an independent appraiser's report and a notarized list of property.
required_dossiers: Bank certificate of deposit balance or balance confirmation
Capital contribution schedule approved by the members
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Independent valuation report for in-kind contributions, if any
Identification documents of the account signatories
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses to open the account because the public-interest permit is still pending, request a provisional or escrow-class account and convert it after authorization. If the balance certificate has insufficient details, obtain a same-day updated certificate indicating the account holder is YUHANG HOESA.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Incorporation Registration with the District Court Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registration Division of the District Court Registry Office having territorial jurisdiction over the registered office, for example the Seoul Central District Court Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the Application for Registration of Incorporation of Yuhan Hoesa to the court registry together with notarized Articles, proof of capital payment, address proof, and identification documents. The court registrar will examine statutory form, legality of purpose, and representative's authority. Upon approval, the court enters the Company into the corporation register and assigns a unique company registration number. Pay the registration tax and education surcharge at the court stamp counter. The effective incorporation date is the date the registration is completed. Request concurrent certified copies of the registration and a sealed certificate of the corporate seal for subsequent filings.
required_dossiers: Completed Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Limited Liability Company
Notarized Articles of Incorporation original
Bank certificate of capital contribution payment
Power of attorney and applicant identification
Registration tax and court fee payment voucher
Corporate seal registration card application
Public-interest establishment authorization from the competent ministry, if obtained
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the court registrar issues a correction order, respond within the stated period, usually two weeks, with corrected documents and any additional fee payments. If the application is rejected, cure all defects and file a new application or file an immediate appeal under the Non-Contentious Case Litigation Act, whichever is procedurally appropriate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain the Business Registration Certificate and Tax Compliance Status
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: District Tax Office under the National Tax Service of the Republic of Korea having jurisdiction over the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After registry incorporation, file a Corporate Business Registration Application with the National Tax Service within one month after commencement of business. Submit the certificate of registered corporation, Articles, and representative identification to obtain a legal entity business registration certificate and corporate tax number. For a charitable endowment entity, apply for tax exemption or public-interest corporation income tax status under the Tax Incentive Limitation Act if eligible. You must also register as a grant-making legal entity able to issue donation receipts under the relevant donation encouragement legislation. This step engages post-filing tax compliance and annual filing obligations.
required_dossiers: Certificate of registered corporation issued by the court registry
Corporate seal certificate
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Lease agreement or proof of registered office address
Representative's identification card
Application for Corporate Business Registration
Public-interest authorization certificate, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office flags discrepancies, provide a written explanation, corrected Articles, or updated court certificates. If a tax-exemption application is denied, seek administrative review before the National Tax Service or appeal to the Tax Tribunal within the statutory deadline.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Public-Interest Foundation Establishment Authorization and Register as an Endowment Manager
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Competent supervising ministry with jurisdiction over the primary purpose, such as the Ministry of Strategy and Finance, the Ministry of Science and ICT, or the Ministry of Education, together with the Financial Supervisory Service if the endowment is invested in regulated financial instruments
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an application for public-interest corporation establishment authorization to the competent supervising ministry with jurisdiction over the primary purpose, such as scientific grants, education, or general charitable endowment. Include the endowment management plan, grant-making procedures, investment policy, audit plan, and a three-year budget. The ministry will examine the public-interest nature, sufficiency of the endowment, sound financial management, and governance. After approval, apply for public-interest registration and update the court registry if any officer changes. If the endowment is invested in financial instruments, comply with the Financial Investment Services and Capital Markets Act and the FSS supervisory framework, and ensure that no unauthorized fund-raising or solicitation of donations is conducted.
required_dossiers: Public-interest corporation establishment application
Legalized and notarized Articles of Incorporation
Endowment asset proof such as bank certificate or trust deed
Project and grant-making plan
Three-year projected budget and endowment investment policy
Officer candidate resumes and background declarations
Court registry certificate and business registration certificate
AML/KYC and grant distribution compliance policy
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the ministry rejects or conditions the authorization, submit a supplementary justification and amend the Articles, endowment plan, or budget. If the ministry requests narrower beneficiary definitions or stricter investment limits, revise the governance documents accordingly. Administrative decisions may be appealed under the Administrative Litigation Act within ninety days of receipt of the written decision.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - no physical manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing operation is being formed under ISIC 6430; the relevant authorities are judicial and financial regulators rather than an industrial licensing board.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable - no factory or warehouse operating permit is required; the statutory authorization is the public-interest corporation establishment permit under the Act on Establishment and Operation of Public Interest Corporations.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable - Ministry of Environment; no EIA screening or environmental permit is required for office-based endowment and grant management under ISIC 6430.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable - the activity does not involve physical development, manufacturing, chemical processing, or waste release and therefore does not trigger any environmental impact assessment tier under the Environmental Impact Assessment Act.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - no process wastewater, VOCs, air emissions, or hazardous waste streams are generated by a charitable endowment management office; only ordinary office waste collection applies.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable - no factory, chemical process, warehouse, or assembly line requiring Civil Defense fire permits is present. The general office space must still obtain an ordinary building fire-safety inspection certificate from the local fire station and comply with the Occupational Safety and Health Act on office workspace safety, emergency evacuation, and fire prevention.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of South Korea; online portal: HomeTax (https://www.hometax.go.kr)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Korean domestic entity such as a Yuhan Hoesa, the procedure begins with obtaining a Business Registration Certificate. The company must submit a business registration application (Business Registration Application Form) to the local district tax office having jurisdiction over the registered place of business, either online through HomeTax or in person. Supporting documents include the Certificate of Incorporation, Articles of Incorporation, lease contract or proof of place of business, copy of the representative's identification, and any required corporate governance resolutions. For foreign non-resident entities with no domestic place of business but with business activities giving rise to Korean tax obligations, the same business registration application is filed through an authorized domestic tax representative; the NTS then assigns a 10-digit Business Registration Number (TIN/VAT ID). If the non-resident entity only has Korean-source income subject to withholding and no VAT obligation, a separate simplified TIN may be issued for withholding tax administration. For a domestic Yuhan Hoesa, the NTS verifies the application and issues the Business Registration Certificate, which simultaneously registers the entity for corporate income tax and Value Added Tax purposes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. A Yuhan Hoesa is not eligible for any check-the-box election under Korean tax law. Hybrid mismatch rules are addressed under the Adjustment of International Taxes Act, but no elective entity-classification regime exists in Korea.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No monetary threshold. Every person supplying taxable goods or services in South Korea is required to register as a VAT taxpayer. Simplified taxpayers with annual gross revenue below KRW 80 million remain registered but are subject to simplified VAT computation rules.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Electronic tax invoices are mandatory under the VAT Act. Every VAT-registered business must issue electronic tax invoices (Electronic Tax Invoice) for B2B supplies and transmit them to the NTS HomeTax system. Transmission must be completed by the day following the invoice issuance date, and the system validates invoices through the NTS electronic tax invoice infrastructure. There is no independent anti-fraud digital stamping requirement equivalent to Italian or Romanian fiscal clearance, but real-time integrity verification is performed by the NTS. Non-compliance attracts VAT penalties and electronic invoice submission penalties.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is available under the VAT Act for the export of goods, where the goods are actually exported from South Korea under a customs export declaration. Services supplied to non-residents or foreign jurisdictions may also be zero-rated if the services are treated as supplied outside Korea or in connection with export goods. A charitable endowment entity claiming export zero-rating must prove that the supply constitutes an export transaction and that the consideration is received from outside Korea in foreign currency.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Export Declaration accepted by Korea Customs Service)
Bill of Lading (or Air Waybill for airfreight exports)
Inward Remittance Certificate / Foreign Exchange Receipt Confirmation issued by a Korean authorized foreign exchange bank
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The NTS may retrospectively adjust any zero-rated export supply if the required evidence is not maintained or if the foreign exchange is not repatriated within the statutory deadline. Unsupported zero-rating gives rise to a VAT assessment equal to the unpaid VAT plus an additional tax of 10% to 30% depending on the nature and severity of the non-compliance. Fraudulent claims may result in criminal penalties under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, including imprisonment or fines, and the statute of limitations for a false export claim is generally extended to 5 years. Repeated or materially false declarations may trigger customs export verification audits and disqualification from future zero-rating privileges.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) in conjunction with the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) as the Foreign Exchange Administration under Chapter 4 of the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act (FXT Act)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea operates a floating exchange rate regime under current account convertibility. Current account receipts, including export proceeds, dividends, interest and unilateral transfers, are freely convertible at the market rate without quantitative limits, provided the transaction is reported to the licensed bank under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. Capital account transactions, however, are subject to declarative control: foreign financial loans, equity contributions and derivative transactions require registration with the MOEF or delegated banks, and certain short-term external borrowings face ceilings. A private charitable foundation receiving foreign grants must classify them as current transfers or donations, which are reportable but not license-restricted, since the underlying purpose is nonprofit. Profit remittance hurdles are minimal but documentary: a liquidating or capital reduction remittance requires tax clearance certificates from the National Tax Service; any grant disbursement to foreign beneficiaries requires underlying award contracts and CRS/FATCA declarations. The KRW is not freely deliverable offshore; settlement of cross-border grants must occur through an onshore foreign currency account at a domestic licensee. As of the current statutory framework, Korea does not impose a surrender ratio on export proceeds; however, exporters must receive the full invoice amount within the prescribed collection period, typically six months from the export license date, and any uncollected balance must be reported as a claim. Overall, convertibility is high on the current account and conditional on compliance on the capital account.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under Articles 19-21 of the FXT Act and Bank of Korea regulations, exporters must collect export proceeds within 6 months from the date of export declaration; an extension of up to 3 additional months is possible for vessel or aircraft construction, overseas works and other MOEF-approved cases. There is no mandatory conversion ratio to KRW; the exporter may retain the foreign currency receipts in a Foreign Currency Deposit Account (FCDA) at a licensed domestic bank, but must report the proceeds to the foreign exchange bank and surrender the full amount for conversion to KRW if the bank determines it is necessary for trade settlement balance. Reports are filed through the bank's electronic Foreign Exchange Information System.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Basic Operational Currency Account (KRW Current Account + Foreign Currency Deposit Account)
Capital Escrow Account for Endowment Grants
Basic Operational Currency Account and Grant Disbursement Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low — foreign fintech EMIs such as Wise or Revolut are not licensed to service South Korean corporations because the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and the Electronic Financial Transactions Act require all foreign exchange business to be conducted through domestic licensed banks; these EMIs lack permissible foreign exchange brokerage licensing for non-resident entities and cannot operate as banks within the jurisdiction. They may only function as engineered referral partners or provide pre-funded debit cards through a licensed Korean bank partner, so they cannot serve as the primary treasury settlement rail for this foundation. All cross-border grant flows must execute via SWIFT through a commercial bank with a domestic reporting duty.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Under Financial Intelligence Unit guidance and the Banking Business Act, at least one statutory director with registered corporate seal must appear physically at the bank branch for the corporate KYC interview. Remote consular proxy opening is not accepted for foreign directors unless the director holds an Alien Registration Card and a domestic telephone number is verified. Non-resident directors may appoint a local agent through a notarized power of attorney with apostille, but the authorised local representative must still undergo an in-branch identity check. A video interview may supplement but can never replace the physical appearance for a private charitable foundation classified as low-AML-risk.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity caused by donor-funded endowment without clear donor identity or source of wealth documentation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copy of the internal UBO register, statutory donation contracts, legal entity chart of each material donor, audited financial statements for the past three years, and public charity registration certificate issued by the National Tax Service and the Ministry of Economy and Finance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound cross-border wire transfers from countries on the Financial Action Task Force grey list or with high unintended tax event risks.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Source of wealth and source of funds letters for every material donor, original bank statements tracing the remittance origin, tax residency certificates and FATCA/CRS self-certification forms, completed AML risk assessment questionnaire, and negative media and sanctions screening reports from LexisNexis or Dow Jones.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual grant disbursement pattern to non-profit beneficiaries in higher-risk jurisdictions or with frequent split payments.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Grant agreement with programme milestones, beneficiary KYC file containing certificates of incorporation, board resolution accepting the grant, CV and passport of authorised beneficiary signatories, an undertaking disclaiming any onward transfer, and a post-disbursement utilisation report demonstrating grant purpose alignment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Concern that the charitable foundation is utilised to circumvent inheritance or gift taxes through donor-directed investments.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copy of charitable foundation status approval under the Income Tax Act and the Endowment Fund Management Guidelines, corporate bylaws prohibiting private benefit, annual grant disbursement ratio reports, management letter from a Korean certified public accountant, and five years of grant distribution records.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All foreign grant and contribution wires must enter through a licensed foreign exchange bank in Korea. The sending institution transmits SWIFT MT103 with field 70 (Remittance Information) quoting 'Charitable Grant - Yuhan Hoesa Foundation' and a purpose classification of 'current unilateral transfer' in the Korean Foreign Exchange Information System. The receiving bank verifies that the remitter is a qualified donor, then credits the non-resident foreign currency account or converts to KRW at the market rate. For endowment principal exceeding USD 500,000, the foundation must file a report with the MOEF through the bank within 20 business days; capital verification is evidenced by a certificate of receipt issued by the bank, matching the remitted amount to the foundation's signed donor agreement and board endowment resolution.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound grant payments and subsidiary trade settlements clear via SWIFT MT103 through the domestic bank's correspondent network. For larger procurement operations, the bank issues Commercial Letters of Credit under ICC UCP 600 with SWIFT MT700 and payment at sight against compliant shipping documents. Documentary Collections (D/P and D/A) are used for low-value or repeat grant purchases where invoice-level control suffices. Every disbursement exceeding KRW 50 million is archived with the underlying grant contract, proforma invoice, board resolution and beneficiary utilisation certificate for at least six years, and every payment is screened against the FIU sanctions list and international restrictive measures databases.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable KRW/USD forward contracts with a licensed domestic bank, not exceeding 12 months, executed against actual or pipeline grant income and foreign-denominated operational expenses

Cross-currency swap agreements to convert long-term USD-denominated endowment bonds into KRW cash flows, subject to Financial Investment Services and Capital Markets Act licensing and underlying exposure verification

Offshore non-deliverable forwards for hedging non-convertible emerging market grant currencies only when cleared through a licensed international broker and documented with a MOEF derivative confirmation, because domestic Korean derivative rules prohibit NDFs for speculative positions

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return and Self-Assessment for Foundation Income and Endowment Gains
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service of the Republic of Korea via the HomeTax electronic filing system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a December 31 fiscal year end, no later than March 31 of the following year; for a non-calendar fiscal year, within 3 months after the fiscal year end, with a possible 1-month extension approved by the National Tax Service
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing penalty of 20% of the unpaid corporate tax; underreporting penalty of 10% (40% for fraudulent underreporting); daily late-payment interest of 0.022% on the unpaid amount from the statutory due date; chronic non-compliance may lead to asset seizure, criminal referral under the Punishment of Tax Evasion Act, and court-ordered dissolution upon request of the national tax authority; no automatic administrative strike-off exists under Korean company law.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements, External Auditor's Report and Audit Exemption Evidence
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service; Financial Supervisory Service through the DART public disclosure portal when a statutory external audit is mandatory; also filed with the competent government grant authority for charitable foundations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The financial statements must be approved by the annual general meeting within 3 months after fiscal year end, generally by March 31 for calendar-year entities, and must be attached to the corporate income tax return; if a statutory external audit applies, the auditor's report must be delivered to the Financial Supervisory Service and the National Tax Service within 45 days after the external auditor issues the report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: For audit-required entities, failure to submit the external audit report may incur administrative fines up to KRW 30,000,000 (approximately USD 22,000) per violation under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies; for a charitable foundation, failure to file audited or inspectable financial statements may suspend tax-deductible contribution eligibility and expose the foundation to corrective orders, funding freezes, or revocation of its public-interest status.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Charitable Foundation Annual Report on Grant Disbursements, Endowment Management, Beneficiaries and Budget Execution
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Competent government authority which granted the foundation's incorporation permit under the Korean Civil Act (which may be the Ministry of Strategy and Finance, Ministry of Education, Ministry of Health and Welfare, Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism, or the provincial/metropolitan government such as Seoul Metropolitan Government, depending on the original license)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after the close of each fiscal year, generally by March 31 for a calendar-year foundation; the upcoming year's budget and grant plan must be pre-filed with the same competent authority at the start of the fiscal year, not later than January 31
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or false reporting permits the competent authority to issue corrective orders, impose administrative fines under the Civil Act, suspend the foundation's grant-making operations, withdraw approval to receive tax-deductible contributions, and in egregious cases institute proceedings for involuntary dissolution through the prosecutor's office; no automatic administrative strike-off exists, but sustained non-compliance can result in judicial dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Commercial Registry Amendment Filings for Reappointment or Change of Directors, Foundation Officers, Registered Office and Authorized Purposes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Registration Section of the district court registry in the district where the Yuhan Hoesa's registered executive office is located
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 14 days (2 weeks) of the date of the annual general meeting resolution or the triggering corporate event; if the articles of incorporation are amended, the registered amendment must also be recorded within 14 days of the resolution
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or omitted registration can expose the corporation to court-imposed minor penalties of up to KRW 5,000,000 (approximately USD 3,700); an unregistered change cannot be asserted against bona fide third parties, leaving the foundation potentially liable on acts of former officers; repeated failure to maintain accurate registry records may be considered by the court in dissolution or regulatory sanction proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Local Corporate Income Surtax Return and Payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local government treasury of the Si/Gun/Gu in which the foundation's registered head office is situated, filed through the national local tax e-tax system Wetax operated by the Ministry of the Interior and Safety
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a December 31 fiscal year end, no later than March 31 of the following year, matching the national corporate income tax filing deadline
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or pay the local surtax triggers a 3% late-payment surcharge after the filing deadline, plus daily late-payment interest of 0.022%; the local government may conduct a compulsory collection against the foundation's bank accounts and assets within one month of delinquency and may restrict the foundation's eligibility for local subsidies or public-interest support programs.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under Article 2 of the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, an independent certified public accountant audit is mandatory for a Yuhan Hoesa (limited liability company) or incorporated foundation when total assets shown on the balance sheet at the end of the immediately preceding fiscal year exceed KRW 12,000,000,000 (approximately USD 8.9 million at an exchange rate of KRW 1,350 per USD). Korean external-audit regulation does not use turnover or employee headcount alone as a statutory audit trigger; however, the competent government authority under the Civil Act may require a statutory audit of a private charitable foundation if annual operating receipts, public donations, or endowment-management turnover exceed KRW 300,000,000 (approximately USD 222,000) or if the foundation has been designated as a public-interest corporation collecting tax-deductible contributions. A foundation with 100 or more full-time employees must also undergo a separate labor compliance audit under Ministry of Employment and Labor regulations, but this is not the same as the financial statement audit required by the External Audit Act. Any mandatory financial audit must be performed by an independent external auditor registered with the Korean Institute of Certified Public Accountants and subject to the Korean Auditing Standards.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: For statutory externally audited entities, financial statements must be prepared in accordance with Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS); for smaller private corporations and charitable foundations, the company may apply Korean Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (K-GAAP); regardless of which general framework applies, charitable endowment transactions and grant distributions must also be booked in conformity with the Accounting Standards for Non-Profit Organizations (K-NPO) and all statements must be prepared on the accrual basis with a statement of financial position, statement of activities, statement of changes in endowment funds, and statement of cash flows.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Korean law does not maintain a standalone annual UBO filing for a private unlisted Yuhan Hoesa foundation; instead, the foundation must continuously update its statutory register of members and the Register of Beneficial Owners or comparable contribution ledger whenever a membership interest, share, or endowment right changes. A transfer of membership interest takes legal effect only when recorded in the statutory register, and the transferee cannot exercise voting or distribution rights until the register has been updated. Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, any acquisition or transfer involving a non-resident investor or foreign beneficiary that crosses or departs from the 10% foreign-investment notification threshold must be reported to an authorized foreign exchange bank and the Directorate General for International Finance within 30 days of the trigger event; separate reporting obligations apply when a public-interest foundation grants a foreign charitable distribution exceeding the cash-transaction reporting threshold under the Financial Transaction Reports Act. The statutory representative must annually confirm, as at the annual general meeting date, that the register of members, register of beneficial owners, and register of grant beneficiaries are complete and true; this confirmation is signed and retained in the minute book and is submitted as part of the corporate income tax return if the foundation claims tax-exempt contribution status.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Foundation Officers and Corporate Secretary
Register of Charges, Mortgages, Pledges, and Endowment Liens
Minute Book of Annual General Meetings and Board Resolutions
Register of Grants, Beneficiaries, and Charitable Disbursements

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 300 - USD 1,200 per annum for a compliant registered executive office and corporate secretarial agent in Seoul, with lower-end pricing in provincial jurisdictions; includes registered address, mail handling, board meeting support, and registry coordination
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,000 - USD 7,000 for a limited-scope compilation or review if the foundation remains below the statutory external-audit threshold; USD 12,000 - USD 30,000 for a full K-IFRS or K-NPO statutory audit, depending on asset size, transaction volume, and the degree of grant monitoring required.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 9% to 24% progressive national corporate income tax: 9% on taxable income up to KRW 200 million; 19% on KRW 200 million to KRW 20 billion; 21% on KRW 20 billion to KRW 300 billion; 24% above KRW 300 billion, plus a 10% local income tax surtax on the national corporate tax (aggregate headline range from 9.9% to 26.4%).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Korean resident charitable endowment corporations that qualify as public-interest non-profit corporations under the Corporate Tax Act are taxed only on income derived from profit-making businesses; donations, grant income, and investment returns allocated to statutory public-interest purposes can be exempt or deductible to specified limits. Additional relief includes tax credits for qualifying research and development expenses, special deductions for social contribution and charitable grant expenditure, and exemption for recognized non-profit activities. No general patent box applies to philanthropic endowment vehicles.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Tax Standard Return for Domestic Corporations (Corporate Tax Tax Base and Tax Return, Form 1) filed electronically through the National Tax Service HomeTax portal (www.hometax.go.kr).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: On or before the last day of the third month following the fiscal year-end; for a calendar-year Yuhan Hoesa, the filing deadline is March 31 of the following year. One additional month may be granted through an extension application.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reporting entity, fiscal year, corporate registration number, business place, and responsible representative details.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the Korean legal entity name and corporate registration number. For a non-resident-owned Yuhan Hoesa, attach the foreign shareholder register, foreign beneficial ownership declaration, and Korean place-of-management records. The Korean foundation must prove that central management and control, board meetings, asset custody decisions, and grant-making approvals occur in Korea to avoid recharacterization as a foreign-controlled paper entity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total revenue and gross receipts from all business and commercial activities.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include investment income from endowment assets, capital gains, management fees, and any ancillary commercial activities. Contributions and grants received for qualified public-interest charitable purposes may be excluded from taxable income only if specifically permitted by Korean tax law and evidenced by donation contracts, grant agreements, and board resolutions. Korean-source income generated by foreign donations remains taxable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible expenses, charitable distributions, and operating costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Grant disbursements, custodial fees, professional advisory fees, and administrative overhead are deductible when supported by contemporaneous documentation. Cross-border payments to related foreign fund managers, advisers, or grantees must satisfy the arm's-length principle and must be reported under transfer-pricing schedules. Expenses without service evidence, exempt-purpose tracing, or proper withholding are disallowed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax-base adjustments, non-deductible expenditures, reserves, and book-tax reconciliation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Add back non-qualifying donations, penalty surcharges, entertainment expenses, political contributions, and excessive related-party payments. Deduct permitted nonprofit reserves only when the statutory conditions are met. If the foundation pays management or royalty fees to a non-resident related party, the Korean payor must apply the correct withholding rate and document the beneficial owner; otherwise the deduction is denied and additional withholding penalties apply.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income computation, loss carryforward, and non-profit charitable exemption schedules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute the taxable base after applying the 10-year loss carryforward. Losses from exempt activities cannot offset taxable investment income, and offshore losses of a non-resident parent or sister entity cannot be deducted by the Korean foundation. A public-interest charitable foundation must demonstrate that any claimed exemption is aligned with its registered articles, actual grant activity, and Korean public-interest use requirements.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Application of national corporate tax rates, progressive tax calculation, foreign tax credits, and total national corporate tax liability.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the progressive Korean corporate tax bands and compute the separate 10% local income tax surcharge. Claim foreign tax credits only where the foreign income has borne foreign tax and a tax treaty or domestic tax law permits the credit. Foreign shareholders' dividend withholding is not reported in this box but in the separate non-resident withholding tax return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Transfer pricing return schedule and related-party international transaction disclosure.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose all cross-border transactions with foreign related parties, including investment management fees, grant management services, lending for endowment purposes, and intellectual property licenses. Where the Local File threshold of KRW 5 billion or Master File threshold of KRW 50 billion is exceeded, attach contemporaneous transfer-pricing documentation, comparability analysis, and the selected arm's-length method. Failure to attach exposes the foundation to transfer-pricing adjustment and penalty tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-resident ownership statements, foreign subsidiary disclosure, and CFC schedules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the Yuhan Hoesa controls a foreign subsidiary or foreign charitable vehicle, disclose the foreign subsidiary and consider Korean Controlled Foreign Corporation rules. Non-resident shareholders must be identified in supplementary schedules for withholding tax compliance. The foundation should also confirm whether any foreign grant or endowment contribution creates a foreign-source or Korean-source classification issue for DTA application.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file the annual corporate tax return by the statutory deadline attracts a non-report penalty equal to 20% of the unpaid tax. Underreported income or overstated deductions generate a penalty tax of 10% of the underreported amount, increased to 40% for fraudulent or intent-driven misreporting. Late payment accrues a daily surcharge approximating 0.03% of the unpaid corporate tax and local income tax. Criminal tax evasion under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act can result in imprisonment up to 3 years or fines up to 5 times the evaded tax, in addition to public disclosure, travel bans, and obstruction of future tax clearances.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 20% statutory withholding tax at the national level payable on dividends distributed by a Korean corporation to a non-resident corporate or individual shareholder, plus the 10% local income tax surcharge resulting in an aggregate statutory withholding rate of 22%, unless the rate is reduced under an applicable Double Tax Treaty.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To apply for treaty relief, the Korean payer must obtain and submit to the National Tax Service: (i) a Tax Residency Certificate issued by the residence jurisdiction of the non-resident shareholder and apostilled or consularized as required; (ii) a detailed beneficial ownership declaration showing that the shareholder is the true owner of the dividend, interest, or royalty, has the right to control and enjoy the income, and is not a pass-through or conduit; (iii) a treaty application form filed through HomeTax before or at the time of payment; and (iv) supporting financial statements or grant documentation where relevant. If treaty relief is requested after tax has been withheld, the non-resident may file a refund claim with the National Tax Service; however, the beneficial ownership requirement is strictly enforced and substance failures will trigger the full 22% rate plus penalties.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding for interest and royalty payments to non-residents is 20% national withholding plus 2% local surcharge, for an aggregate statutory rate of 22%. Applicable tax treaties may reduce the rate, commonly to 10% for interest and 10% to 15% for royalties depending on the treaty partner. Reduced treaty rates are available only if the non-resident recipient provides a Tax Residency Certificate, holds beneficial ownership, and satisfies the relevant limitation-on-benefits or treaty-abuse provisions.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File must be prepared and maintained where cross-border intercompany transactions with a foreign related party exceed KRW 5 billion; Master File is required where total cross-border related-party transactions exceed KRW 50 billion; a Country-by-Country Report is required when the ultimate parent group's consolidated revenue is KRW 1 trillion or more. Failure to maintain or submit such documentation can trigger penalties, evidentiary burdens, and transfer-pricing adjustments.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea does not apply a Gulf-style Economic Substance Regulations regime, but the Corporate Tax Act and general anti-avoidance rules enforce a substance-over-form doctrine. The Yuhan Hoesa must perform Core Income-Generating Activities in Korea, including asset custody, grant approval, investment management, risk control, and board oversight. A Korean charitable foundation that is merely a pass-through mailbox entity with decisions made offshore can be disregarded, re-characterized, or treated as having a foreign place of effective management, resulting in higher tax exposure, penalty taxes, and denial of nonprofit benefits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and Fraudulent Charitable Claim
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Fabricating donation records, inflating grant disbursements, funneling business profits through the Yuhan Hoesa to obtain a non-profit tax exemption, or issuing false grant contracts to related foundations for the purpose of shifting income tax-free to shareholders or affiliated persons.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act and the Corporate Tax Act, the National Tax Service may impose additional taxes of 10% to 40% of the underreported income, a 20% non-filing penalty, and daily late-payment surcharges. Criminal tax evasion is punishable by imprisonment up to 3 years and fines up to 5 times the amount of tax evaded.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Korean courts may pierce the corporate veil under the Korean Commercial Act, making directors jointly and severally liable for the corporation's tax obligations and damages caused to creditors and shareholders. Directors involved in the scheme face personal civil restitution, asset freezes, restrictions on departure from Korea through blacklisting and travel bans for substantial delinquencies, disqualification from charitable governance, and criminal imprisonment under the Criminal Act for breach of trust or fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing and Thin Capitalization Misconduct
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Executing cross-border related-party arrangements with foreign parent entities, affiliates, or overseas charitable vehicles at non-arm's-length prices, including excessive management fees, artificial royalties, unsubstantiated intercompany loans, or disguised capital contributions, and failing to prepare the standard transfer-pricing documentation required by Korean law.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The National Tax Service may recharacterize the transaction, adjust taxable income to the arm's-length result, deny non-arm's-length deductions, impose penalty tax under the Corporate Tax Act for international transaction violations, and levy daily late-payment surcharges. Documentation failures may additionally trigger information-reporting penalties and evidentiary burdens against the taxpayer.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approve sham or mispriced related-party transactions are personally liable for the resulting corporate tax deficiencies and civil damages under Korean Commercial Act principles. The corporate veil may be pierced where the charity is undercapitalized, controlled solely by the shareholder, and used as a vehicle to avoid tax. Directors may be subject to criminal charges for unlawful diversion of assets, travel bans, blacklisting, and imprisonment where the transaction amounts to embezzlement or breach of fiduciary duty.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML/CFT, Sanctions, and Illicit Grant Distribution
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the charitable endowment entity as an unregulated pass-through for anonymous donations from sanctioned jurisdictions, executing bank wires to designated persons or terrorist-linked organizations, failing to conduct counter-party screening, or deliberately ignoring suspicious transactions involving the foundation's bank account.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Act on Reporting and Use of Certain Financial Transaction Information and the Korean criminal law, failure to report suspicious transactions or engaging in money laundering through a charitable foundation can result in imprisonment up to 5 years, penalties up to KRW 50 million, regulatory fines, asset forfeiture, license revocation, and secondary sanctions exposure from international sanctions regimes.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers may be prosecuted for willful blindness and money laundering even where the corporate entity is used as a facade. The corporate veil can be pierced to hold directors personally liable for the repatriation of illicit funds, civil asset recovery, travel bans, blacklisting, disqualification from serving as directors, and criminal imprisonment. The foundation's banking relationships are placed at risk and its tax-exempt status may be revoked.

stage_6.non_resident_tax_declaration_red_flags: Non-resident shareholders and foreign beneficial owners must be fully identified on supplement schedules; outbound payments must be subjected to the correct withholding and treaty procedure; no charitable grant or management payment to a foreign related party may be made solely to avoid Korean tax; and the foundation must maintain robust minutes, substance files, and transfer-pricing documentation for at least five years after the relevant fiscal year.
